name: Hen and Chickens
note: One big rock and a brood of small ones; Cook named a group so in 1769, and charts have many more

name: The Aldermen
note: Cook thought they looked like the Court of Aldermen in session

name: Lookers-On
note: Cook's name for onlookers who kept their distance

name: The Paternosters
note: Jersey's reef, where passing sailors said the Lord's Prayer for those wrecked there

name: Parson and Clerk
note: A tall rock and a short one, after a pair on the Devon coast

name: The Brothers
note: A common chart name for rocks of a size

name: The Sisters
note: A common chart name for islets of a size

name: The Twins
note: Bimini is said to be Lucayan for the twins

name: Seven Sleepers
note: Seven low islets that never stir

name: The Snares
note: Vancouver's name for a group he judged a hazard to shipping

name: The Traps
note: Cook: rock ledges that could catch unwary ships

name: The Snorers
note: Roncadores: Spanish for the reefs that roar

name: The Doldrums
note: Cays in calm water where nothing ever blows

name: Five Fingers
note: Cook: five high rocks like a hand

name: The Tin Isles
note: The Cassiterides: the ancients' tin islands, never certainly found

name: Aurora Isles
note: Phantom islands reported by a Spanish ship in 1762 and never seen again

name: Sow and Pigs
note: A chart name for a big rock and a litter of small ones

name: Cow and Calves
note: A big rock with calves beside it

name: Mare and Foals
note: A big island trailed by small ones

name: Goose and Goslings
note: Low cays in a line behind a bigger one

name: Bread and Butter Cays
note: After a pair of cays in Belize

name: Pieces of Eight
note: Eight cays, one for each real in a Spanish dollar

name: The Ninepins
note: Nine upright rocks, like Hong Kong's Ninepin Group

name: The Skittles
note: Short round stacks standing in a cluster

name: Ducks and Drakes
note: In a line like a stone skipped across water

name: Stepping Stones
note: A string of islets you could almost walk

name: The Chessmen
note: Stacks like chessmen on a board

name: The Gossips
note: The surf chatters among them day and night

name: The Jury
note: Twelve rocks, all of one mind

name: Hare and Hounds
note: One cay ahead and the rest strung out after it

name: The Mourners
note: Dark rocks bowed toward the falls

name: The Whelps
note: Whelps: small rocks around a big one, as the ribs round a capstan

name: The Choir
note: The wind sings in the gaps between them

name: The Fiddlers
note: Islets that seem to dance in the shimmer

name: The Admirals
note: Big, grey and immovable

name: The Bellringers
note: The surf booms in their caves like bells

name: Peas in a Pod
note: Small round cays all alike

name: Three Graces
note: Three fair islands side by side

name: The Hogsheads
note: Round as barrels

name: The Pilgrims
note: In single file across the sea

name: Sea Wolves
note: Rocks that lie in wait
